## What's new in 2.3.0

### Sign-in without Tailscale

FreeReps no longer requires Tailscale. An `auth:` block in `config.yaml` switches on application login:

- **Sign-in** through an OIDC provider, local passwords, or both.
- **Personal access tokens** for everything that is not a browser: the iOS app, Health Auto Export, `freereps-upload` (scope `api`) and MCP clients (scope `mcp`). Create them under **Settings → Account**.
- **Accounts**: an admin flag, disabling a user, and a policy for who may sign in (`closed`, or `oidc_auto` with an optional list of email domains).
- **iOS app 2.3.0**: **Sign In** in the app's settings opens the server's login page and stores a token for that iPhone; **Sign Out** revokes it. **Test Connection** now tells an unreachable address, a server that is not FreeReps, and a rejected sign-in apart.

Nothing changes for an existing installation: without an `auth:` block the server behaves as before, and Tailscale remains the default. Configuration: [README § Access](https://github.com/meltforce/FreeReps#access) and [`server/config.example.yaml`](https://github.com/meltforce/FreeReps/blob/main/server/config.example.yaml).

> [!WARNING]
> **Without Tailscale, securing the connection is your responsibility.** In Tailscale mode the tailnet keeps the server private and encrypts every connection. With `tailscale.enabled: false` FreeReps listens on plain HTTP and can no longer ensure either. Put it behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS, do not publish the plain-HTTP port, and decide yourself who can reach the address. FreeReps holds health data; an instance reachable from the internet is protected by its login alone.

**Upgrading an installation that will switch off Tailscale:** update the server first, then update the iOS app to 2.3.0 and sign in, and only then disable Tailscale. An older app has no way to send a token and is locked out of a server that requires one. While both `auth:` and Tailscale are enabled, a request without a token falls back to the Tailscale identity, so the old app keeps working during the switch.

### openGym integration

New since 2.2.1: FreeReps syncs strength workouts from [openGym](https://github.com/DuarteSantos8/openGym), a self-hosted workout logger. Pair an instance under **Settings → openGym** with a pairing code; the sync runs every 30 minutes, rewrites a workout only when its sets changed, and removes one deleted in openGym. Exercises are mapped onto the existing catalog, so a lift keeps its name and muscle groups when moving over from Hevy. Setup: [README § openGym](https://github.com/meltforce/FreeReps#opengym).

### Also in this release

- **iOS app**: the sync tiles show the rows stored on the server and what the last sync added, instead of a count kept on the phone that started over after a reinstall.
- **Oura workouts with a GPS route** appeared twice, once with the measurements and once with only the map. They are one workout now, and existing pairs are merged by the next Oura sync.
- **Alerts** can be sent in an ntfy format beside the Uptime Kuma JSON object.
- **`/healthz`** reports the status and the build.
- Dependency and Go updates, including security fixes.
